name: outw
synopsis: void outw(unsigned short value, unsigned short port);
description: The outw function performs low-level output of a 16-bit word to a specified I/O port. It is primarily intended for internal kernel use but can be accessed from user space with proper permissions.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The 16-bit value to write to the I/O port

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port address to write to

return_value.failure: May result in a segmentation fault if I/O permissions are not set

errors.description: Segmentation fault occurs if the process lacks permission to access the I/O ports, typically requiring ioperm(2) or iopl(2)

bugs: Functions require compilation with optimization flags like -O or -O2, as they are defined as inline macros; argument order (value before port) differs from some DOS implementations.
